newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ labour costs rise 2.8 pct in yr to March qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ labour costs rise 2.8 pct in yr to March qtr.

text.p: Labour costs increased by 2.8 percent from the March 1996 quarter to the March 1997 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday in relasing its Labour Cost Index.
This follows increases of 2.5 percent and 2.4 percent for the years to September and December 1996.
SNZ said labour costs rose by 3.4 percent in the public sector and by 2.6 percent in the private sector in the year to March.

"In the year to March 1997, salary and wage rates rose by 2.2 percent. Non-wage labour costs increased by 5.2 percent, with private sector non-wage labour costs rising 5.3 percent and public sector costs going up 4.8 percent," SNZ said.

From the December 1996 quarter to the March 1997 quarter, labour costs rose by 0.7 percent overall, with salary and wage rates (including overtime) rising 0.7 percent and non-wage labour costs increasing by 0.6 percent.

SNZ said the increase in salary and wage rates (up 2.2 percent) accounted for 67 percent of the 2.8 percent annual increase in labour costs, with the remaining 33 percent coming from higher non-wage labour costs (up 5.2 percent).

An increase in ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) employer premium costs accounted for 17 percent of the latest overall annual increase in labour costs, while higher annual leave and statutory holiday costs accounted for 12 percent, SNZ said.
